But after our last witness, you could see that I don't want to broaden the issue. It is only to focus on the facts that still cause some suspicion. That is why I abided by the suggestions given to us by Your Honours during yesterday's conference, and I shall continue along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We said yesterday no duplication, triplication of the evidence, and you don't need to support the evidence of the Prosecution's own witness, particularly when he was the commander of the fourth corps, a member, and he was already in the fighting in Mostar during the earlier months. We should know what the structure of the army was during the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, since we have clarified your role in the Oganj Operation, and I think that the facts have been clarified sufficiently, I'm not going to ask you any more questions about that operation and about the role of Zejnil Delalic in it. However, I'm going to ask you whether you know as a member of the joint command who at that time was the head of the anti-aircraft defence in the joint command and in the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. It was Enver Redzepovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether at any point after he became the head of the anti-aircraft defence Mr. Redzepovic was either relieved of his duty or changed his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, can you tell me whether you know if Zejnil Delalic at any period of time in 1992, according to the information that you have, at the time when he had no command role whatsoever was still engaged in assisting the struggle with his own personal means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that what is the most characteristic is that with his own personal means, he bought a 130-millimetre gun, and I was present there at the event when he gave the money to a man whose nickname was Srna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were a soldier then and you're still a soldier now, this assistance which Mr. Delalic provided to the defence forces, was it a significant kind of help for the defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, any assistance was extremely useful to us, so that was very useful to us as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it the same gun that the TO refused to give to Delalic when he asked for it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you personally know with respect to this gun, and the court already has information that this gun was nicknamed Sultan, so was there any problem with the HVO regarding this gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When this gun arrived on that very day and I was present when this money was counted, members of the HVO took away the spare parts and tools, so the sights, there were the cleaning equipment and other things which were necessary for the gun to function. So, they simply took it off the truck and took it somewhere away. I did not see this, but a lot of people came to see this gun, both military and civilians, but I was not there. I know that after that there were certain problems arose.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the security body of the municipal staff take some measures against certain members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. The security authorities forbid them to approach our warehouses because they thought that if they had taken this away we couldn't use that gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Pasic, we will move on to another area. Do you whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic at, some time in 1992, was appointed a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. After the Oganj Operation, so it was in later July or early August, I heard that he was appointed to the position of the commander of Tactical Group 1. This is what I have heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this gun called Sultan, part of the artillery weapons which you commanded over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It became a weapon of the municipal staff. I was commander of the joint, that is, mixed artillery division, but it belonged to the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, after the request to transfer this gun to the Tactical Group, a conflict broke out with the municipal staff. Can you tell me whether you know from your personal experience that you yourself and the municipal staff did not want to turn this gun over to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were problems over this. Personally as a commander, I had a problem because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ultimately, the dispute was referred to the supreme commander and he said that he directed that the gun should be given to TG-1. We already have evidence on that. You can ask him whether when all formations were placed at the disposal of TG-1, was his unit also placed under this command? You can ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have understood His Honour's comment. Is it true that you turned this gun over after Commander Sefer Halilovic ordered it be turned over; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me even though, Mr. Pasic, you turned this gun over, was your combined artillery division subordinate to Mr. Zejnil Delalic as commander of Tactical Group 1, that is, to the command of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. My division was subordinate to the municipal staff of the Konjic defence forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, did you personally as a soldier and member of the Territorial Defence of Konjic at any time subordinate to Mr. Zejnil Delalic as commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, were you at any other time under any other commander subordinate to the commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, do you know that a number of soldiers of the Gijret unit were subordinate to the Tactical Group 1 in the month of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that. I think this was in the month of June during the first attempt at lifting the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the first attempt at lifting the siege was over, do you know under whose command the soldiers who came back from Konjic were placed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The soldiers were going back to the original units from which they came and they were sent to other tasks. That included the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, do you know that after the combat operations at Bradina, a certain number of persons who took part in the fighting were detained and taken to the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether any person whom you knew was detained and taken to the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I knew several persons who apparently were in Celebici. Members of their families came to me asking me to try to find out what happened to them; for instance, Ranko Glogovac was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, did you do something at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did what I could. I thought that my duty as a human being was to try to help because I thought that not all people were either armed or Chetniks, and I specifically helped Ranko. I grew up with Goran Lokas and I asked him to have him released. Several days later, I saw that he had come home.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was approximately late May or early June.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, can you please tell me whether in your artillery division combined, as you said it was called, whether Mladen Zebic was also there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He was in the joint staff so he was my deputy, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, was he in any way connected to the theft of the spare parts and tools for the Sultan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: These questions, what are they about? What are these questions intended to establish?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Certain documents presented here were actually propaganda against Zejnil, and I'm laying the foundation for showing that they were propaganda. Since this witness can elucidate some aspects of it, I wanted him to talk to some of the elements which he can speak to, but if you believe that this issue has been sufficiently clarified, the witness need not answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, and towards the case of his defence. That's all we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the Prosecution may have also relied on certain documents which were part of this smearing campaign. We would like to show in defence of our client that he was framed on those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone not on)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, I would also like to ask you whether you know, given the position that you occupied, whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic, either as coordinator or commander of Tactical Group 1, had any authority over the Celebici barracks and prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I know, he had no authority. It would have been impossible for him to have had any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, on the basis of your personal knowledge, do you know whether any guard at the Celebici barracks was a member of Tactical Group 1, whether during the tenure of Mr. Polutak or Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really could not speak to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Pasic, this concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point, no. However, with your kind permission, maybe after reviewing all the relevant documents, we may have a couple of questions on Monday of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: After he has been charged, is it? After he has been discharged as a witness? Any cross-examination of him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Defence of Hazim Delic has no questions in cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The prosecution any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, the defence of Esad Landzo has no questions of this witness either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, you say some of the people detained in Bradina were taken to the Celebici barracks, who detained them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: First ask him who arrested them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Arrest or detained.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who arrested them? Do you know who arrested them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that these persons were detained in Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, neither did I. I'm sorry, I think there's been a confusion. You mentioned that people who -- I think you used the word detained in Bradina were sent to Celebici, but people who were arrested in Bradina, if the word "arrested" is correct, they were taken to Celebici, who arrested them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was talking about Ranko Glogovac. He was at Donje Selo that is where he was found. And that is where he was arrested and taken to Celebici. And I believe that it was the MUP who took him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they arrested him and took him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why Mr. Delalic was appointed commander of Tactical Group 1? Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now you mentioned that you're on the joint command and you're on that command with a number of other people. I am just interested, if I have the people that correct -- if I have the correct list of people who are on the joint command. So I'll mention the names and you might tell me if you would be so kind. Was the first commander Enver Redzepovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but he was not my first commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'll just go through the list of the first joint command of the TO and HVO. And then, was there Dinko Zebic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dinko Zebic was the chief of staff at the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Ivan Asanovic was deputy commander, I think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mihat Cerovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mihat Cerovac?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Say, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Jasmin Guska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, no, for Jasmin Guska.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do not understand this line of questioning. My objection is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He wants to find out whether those persons were there or not. He's got a list I think prepared by -- he just wants to check up with that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Those who are member of the joint command, who have been heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this is not the list -- he's giving some names that were -- in other words, we were not provided such a list, which would have been his obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It depends on him to admit or reject.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I can assure, Your Honours, I won't give false names.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then there was a second commander appointed to the joint command and that was Esad Ramic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat this last one, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. After Enver Redzepovic was appointed, the next commander to be appointed was Esad Ramic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And under Esad Ramic, it was when he was the commander of the joint command, that was the time that you were on the joint command, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not exactly. If you want me to explain, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you can give me a yes or no answer, it would be much easier, and then we can finish today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My first commander in actual fact was Omer Boric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I am speaking specifically of the joint command. I am not talking about the TO. I am talking about the joint command -- the commander of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Omer Boric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Now, when you were on the joint command, Zejnil Delalic and Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic was also on the joint command, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness answered this question already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The witness didn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A number of them were members of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to Madam Residovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute, what was the answer he gave?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, he said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: A number of members, a number of them were members of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I thought he was denying it. Neither of the members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please check up on the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now in the statement that you gave --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness should be allowed to state unequivocally, there's your comment, but he has not -- then in the transcript, it is not clear whether operation -- Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic were members of the joint command or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please speak a little loudly, so that the interpreters can know what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic and Zejnil Delalic, a member of the joint command when you were a member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in your statement that you gave to Ms. Residovic, you mentioned a name of Ivan Asanovic, would you like to look at your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you do, please don't hesitate to ask. Now, it's true, isn't it, that in that you refer to Ivan Asanovic and you said that he had the position of being president of the HVO, do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: President of the HVO's political body, which corresponds with the war presidency in our army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the war presidency in our army, I don't understand, how do you mean the war presidency in our army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am just quoting from an English translation from what I think it is you've said and I was going to ask you what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the statement in Bosnian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is the statement of the defence, Your Honour. I have a copy here of the statement. I just noticed that the photocopy is very poor, so you may not be able to see it. But, if you can't, we'll move on. Thank you, could you give that to... Now, while we're waiting for that to be distributed, it's true, is it not, that there were ongoing problems between the HVO and the TO during the whole course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no problems at the very beginning. There were no significant problems. We functioned well together up until the Oranj Operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, is it your evidence that after the Oranj Operation and, in particular, after the seizing of the equipment relating to the, to the 130 millimetre gun, that's when relations began the deteriorate rapidly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, immediately after that. The relationships between myself and my deputy sort of cooled off.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is obvious that the sentence which had just been quoted was mistranslated, it's the last paragraph on page 2. As far as Ivan Asanovic is concerned, I know that he was president of the HVO, that is their political body, which would correspond to our war presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There's no reference to the joint staff. It is no reference to the joint staff. It's the position Asanovic. He may also be in the joint command, but you are talking about he was the president of a political party, which corresponds to the position of the war presidency. It is not a reference to the joint staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Which is equivalent to the political body. I see no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only the Prosecutor suggested that the war presidency somehow related to the army, which I say was a mistranslation really.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness might be shown the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, he couldn't be the only one who would translate the war presidency as equivalent to the head of the army. You have too many witnesses indicating, clearly, that the war presidency is a civilian organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's not -- it is nothing to do with my line of questioning, though, Your Honour. My line of questioning relates to the fact that the army had a political master.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And the political master of the army -- and the political master of the army, in the case of the HVO, was a civil -- civilian person who was president of the HVO and that civilian political master corresponded, according to what I can read here, to the president of the war presidency with respect to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He was speaking within the context of his own constitutional structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's what he says here Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I don't think he would say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It appears very clearly from the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, if I can be of some assistance, this is an OTP translation and, in my submission, it's a mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's why I was going to put the statement to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, put it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You must have a better version of the statement because he provided to the Prosecution. You must be having a clearer version of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the original statement and we submitted it to the prosecution, but all in Bosnian, so what I say here is that the translation that was then made was mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Witness, would you endeavour to read, if you can, the paragraph that starts, "As for Ivan Asanovic". Can read that paragraph for me. It's towards the very end. In fact, in the English version, it's the fourth to last paragraph of the whole statement. I believe it's on the last page. I think it's the bottom of the...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let him have your copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is what I was requesting, that you can give him that version, which is probably a clearer one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Give it to him. You don't have to...

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Go to the same place in the statement, would you for me please, four paragraphs towards the end and just read out the statement, which I think should start, "As for Ivan Asanovic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what it is says. "As far as Ivan Asanovic is concerned, I know that he was the president of the HVO, that is their political body which would correspond to our war presidency". I did not -- had any contacts with him, so his activities are not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, fair enough. Now, when you say "war presidency", is the words "in our army" appear there, or do they not appear there? In your statement, you read it so fast, I am just asking you, do the words "after war presidency in our army" appear?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: In our army, war presidency, in our army, are those words in the original text?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there are no such words.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I please have this copy back, it is my personal copy. If necessary, I can provide -- on the other hand, nobody is offering it. We just read a paragraph from it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this copy has been marked and this copy has been shown to the witness, so I should keep it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Give a clean copy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Who said for you to keep it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This copy has not been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Forget it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If Your Honour will permit me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Return it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any re-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, could you please tell me, who was the first commander of the Territorial Defence headquarters of Konjic after April 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After 17 April, the commander was Omer Boric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. After the 17th of April, Esad Ramic, and after the 18th of May, Omer Boric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you absolutely sure of these facts or can you not speak to these facts with full precision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I could not really say exactly because they changed very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But could you tell me who the commander was when you became a member of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Omer Boric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you are absolutely sure of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this is all for this witness. You are discharged. Thank you very much for your assistance to the Trial Chamber. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble on Monday at ten a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
